claims.text: Adding Y and Hf to a NiCoCrAl-type multiprincipal-element alloy induces lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion increases vacancy formation energies.
Lattice distortion increases cation migration barriers, including barriers to Al migration.
Increased vacancy formation energies and migration barriers suppress sustained Al or cation diffusion through the Al-depletion zone.
Suppression of sustained elemental diffusion retards steady-state growth of the protective Al2O3 scale.
Slower steady-state oxide growth enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance and material integrity.
The starting undoped NiCoCrAl-type alloy has a homogeneous composition and a conventional microstructure.
Enhanced lattice strain facilitates rapid formation of the protective Al2O3 scale.
The doped alloy forms an adherent protective Al2O3 scale.
The Y/Hf-doped alloy should have approximately a 60% lower TGO growth rate than an undoped NiCoCrAl-type baseline.
The Y/Hf-doped alloy should resist TGO spallation better than the baseline.
An undoped NiCoCrAl-type baseline forms an Al2O3 scale that grows faster under identical conditions.
The proposed behavior applies from 1100°C to 1200°C in dry air.
The oxidation benefit persists for at least 500 hours at 1200°C.
The hypothesis is limited to dopant levels that produce homogeneous lattice distortion without harmful secondary phases.
Dopant distribution and lattice strain can be assessed using atom probe tomography and high-resolution TEM.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says enhanced lattice strain facilitates rapid Al2O3 formation, while the mechanism says the same distortion suppresses Al transport and slows scale growth. These could describe initial versus steady-state stages, but that temporal distinction is not made in the mediator, and the evidence attributes rapid initial scale formation to the refined eutectic structure rather than to lattice strain.
